source_text: Atque ideo in primo libro nec me fuisse mentitum, qui scripseram omnes, qui fugissent nostrae societatis invidiam, in Manichaeorum praerupta corruere liberum arbitrium denegantium et Deum hominum conditorem teque id, quod fueras propulsare conatus, statim absolutis arripuisse sermonibus etiam illorum scriptorum, quae ad Bonifatium miseras, insertione patefeci [n128] . Verumtamen hoc etiam haec, quam nunc posui, tua responsio confitetur; dixisti enim catholicam fidem esse, quae et liberum credit arbitrium et Deum nascentium conditorem, quod utrumque omnium haereticorum Manichaeos certum est vobiscum negare.
pass_a_gloss: And therefore in the first book I disclosed that I had not lied, who had written that all who had fled the envy of our society fall into the steeps of the Manichaeans denying free choice and God the founder of humans, and that you immediately snatched by absolute speeches that which you had tried to repel, even by the insertion of those writings which you had sent to Boniface. Nevertheless this also this response of yours, which I have now placed, confesses; for you said that it is the catholic faith which both believes free choice and God the founder of those being born, which both among all heretics it is certain the Manichaeans deny with you.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: In the first book, therefore, I showed that I had not lied when I wrote that everyone who fled the stigma of association with us fell over the precipices of the Manichaeans, who deny free will and God as humanity’s creator. I also showed that you immediately embraced, in entirely explicit language, what you had attempted to repel, even quoting the writings you sent to Boniface (see this work 1.14). Yet this answer of yours, which I have just quoted, admits the same thing. You said the catholic faith believes both in free will and in God as the creator of newborn children. Among all heretics, the Manichaeans are certainly the ones who deny both, along with you.

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
